comment: The one-implementation registry: every shared component the product has agreed to build once,
and the single directory it lives in. An entry here is a promise that no second file exports a
symbol of that name, and the check enforces both halves — the home exists, and nothing else
claims the name. Add a component here the moment its contract is agreed, not once it is built:
the whole value is that the name is taken before somebody else takes it.
`pending` marks a home that is being written right now. Its absence is a notice rather than a
failure, and the mark must come off the moment the home lands — an entry excused forever is an
allowancesComment: Pre-existing debt, declared out loud. Every entry here is a REAL violation that predates the
rule catching it: the status register and the placeholder ruling both landed after the code
below was written, and the files belong to slices that are open right now. An allowance is not
a way to make a rule quiet — it is a way to let the rule bite on new work while the debt stays
on screen, printed on every run.
Two things keep the list honest, and they are checked: every entry carries a reason, and an
entry whose violation is gone is itself a failure. So fixing one of these means deleting its
line here in the same commit, and the list can never fill up with entries nobody re-reads.
An entry matches on rule + file + text (line numbers move; the violation does not). For a
placeholder the `text` is the ghost text itself, so changing the wording re-arms the rule.
The alternative escape, for a NEW placeholder that is genuinely right, is the repository's
inline `fitness-allow: <justification>` comment on the line above — a reviewed edit in the
file itself, which is where an argument about one field's wording belongs.
